def factor_volume_synchronized_return(df):
    """Difference in average returns between high- and low-volume days, past 20 days, using classify_volume_regime."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    is_high_vol, is_low_vol, _ = alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime(
        df_copy["volume"], window=20
    )
    daily_ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change().fillna(0)
    high_ret = daily_ret * is_high_vol
    low_ret = daily_ret * is_low_vol
    roll_sum_high = high_ret.rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    roll_cnt_high = is_high_vol.rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    avg_high = (roll_sum_high / roll_cnt_high.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0)
    roll_sum_low = low_ret.rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    roll_cnt_low = is_low_vol.rolling(20, min_periods=1).sum()
    avg_low = (roll_sum_low / roll_cnt_low.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0)
    factor = avg_high - avg_low
    factor = factor.fillna(0)
    df_copy["factor_volume_synchronized_return"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_volume_synchronized_return"]
description: Captures whether the stock tends to perform better on high-volume days relative to low-volume days. High-volume moves are often driven by informed trading or liquidity shocks, so a positive spread indicates that buying pressure accompanies large volume. Uses alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime to identify high/low volume days (thresholds 1.5/0.6, 20-day window). Average returns are computed per regime; when a regime is absent, its contribution is filled with 0 to avoid NaN. The initial NaN from pct_change is also filled with 0.
